title: Save the Egg! Impulse Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Jump onto concrete and it jars your knees. Jump into a sand pit and it feels soft. A fielder pulls his hands back as he catches. And Diya's kitchen challenge: catch a raw egg without breaking it. The egg must lose the same momentum either way, so what changes? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we meet impulse, J = F Δt = Δp.

On a live motion notebook two identical clay balls at 5 m/s are stopped by a hard wall and by a soft cushion, in slow motion, while the readout and a force vs time graph draw together: a tall, thin spike and a low, wide hump with the same area, 1 N s. Four times the stopping time gives a quarter of the average force. Then we derive impulse step by step, see why it is the area under the F-t graph, compare stiff and soft hands side by side, look at sand pits, mats, airbags and bent knees, work through a fielder's catch, see the exam trap (a ball that bounces back does change its momentum), solve an original JEE Main pattern question and finish with a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Save the egg: same stop, different force
0:29 Impulse from F = dp/dt
0:57 Motion notebook: hard wall vs soft cushion
1:38 Impulse in five steps: the area under F-t
2:25 Side by side: stiff vs soft hands + pause and think
3:01 Sand pits, mats, airbags, bent knees + pause and think
3:33 Worked example: the fielder's catch
4:10 Exam trap: the ball that bounces back
4:34 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:19 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Conservation of Linear Momentum. Two carts at rest push apart and fly off. Where does their momentum come from?
